member.name: T:ResxProcessor.Processes
member.summary: Provides utility methods for detecting and synchronizing with other running instances of the current process.
member.remarks: The Processes class enables applications to check for other running instances of themselves and to wait for those instances to exit before proceeding. This can be useful in scenarios where only one instance should perform a particular operation at a time, or where coordination between multiple instances is required. All methods operate on the current process name and compare process start times to distinguish between instances.

member.name: M:ResxProcessor.Processes.WaitSameProcessesStartedEarlier
member.summary: Waits for any other running instances of the current process, with the same name and command-line arguments, to exit before continuing.
member.remarks: This method is useful for ensuring that only one instance of a process with the same name and arguments runs at a time. It blocks execution until all previously started matching processes have exited. If no such processes are found, the method returns immediately.
member.returns: true if the method waited for at least one matching process to exit; otherwise, false.

member.name: M:ResxProcessor.Processes.IsProcessRunning(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether a process with the specified name is currently running, excluding the current process instance.
member.remarks: This method excludes the current process from the search results. If multiple processes with the specified name are running, the first matching process is returned. The caller is responsible for disposing the returned object if necessary.
member.param: The name of the process to search for. This value is case-insensitive and should not include the file extension. Cannot be null or empty.
member.returns: A object representing a running process with the specified name, or if no such process is found.

member.name: T:ResxProcessor.Program
member.summary: Provides the entry point for the application that processes .resx resource files in a specified directory tree, adding a <data> element with the relative file path if it does not already exist.
member.remarks: The application prompts for a root folder if none is specified via command-line arguments. It validates the existence of the folder before proceeding. For each .resx file found, the application checks for a <data> element named "this_FileName" and adds it if missing, storing the file's relative path. The process is intended to be run in environments where multiple instances may be started; synchronization is handled by the Processes class. The application returns 0 on success and 1 if the specified folder does not exist.

member.name: M:ResxProcessor.Program.Main(System.String[])
member.summary: Serves as the entry point for the application, processing resource files in the specified root folder.
member.remarks: The method expects the root folder to exist and contain .resx files to process. If the folder does not exist, an error message is displayed and the application exits with a non-zero code. All .resx files found in the root folder and its subdirectories are processed.
member.param: An array of command-line arguments. The first argument, if provided, specifies the root folder to process. If no arguments are supplied, the user is prompted to enter the root folder path.
member.returns: An integer exit code. Returns 0 if processing completes successfully; returns 1 if the specified folder does not exist.
